events.title: Death of Joseph Smith
events.description: Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, and his brother Hyrum Smith were killed by a mob while being held in Carthage Jail in Illinois.
events.significance: The killings triggered a succession crisis in the Latter Day Saint movement, leading Brigham Young to guide a large group of followers west to Utah.

events.title: First Nuclear Power Plant Connected to a Grid
events.description: The Soviet Union's Obninsk Nuclear Power Plant began supplying electricity to a power grid, becoming the world's first nuclear power station to generate electricity for civilian use on a grid.
events.significance: It marked the beginning of the commercial nuclear energy era and opened the way for nuclear power programs worldwide.

events.title: Birth of Helen Keller
events.description: Helen Keller was born in Tuscumbia, Alabama. Left deaf and blind by illness in infancy, she learned to communicate with the help of teacher Anne Sullivan and went on to graduate from Radcliffe College.
events.significance: Keller became a renowned author, lecturer, and activist for disability rights, women's suffrage, and labor rights, transforming public perceptions of people with disabilities.

events.title: United Nations Security Council Calls for Military Aid to South Korea
events.description: Following North Korea's invasion of South Korea, the UN Security Council adopted a resolution recommending that member states provide assistance to repel the attack, and President Truman ordered US air and sea forces to support South Korea.
events.significance: This action internationalized the Korean War and was a defining moment of early Cold War collective security under the UN.

events.title: First ATM Installed
events.description: The world's first automated teller machine, developed by John Shepherd-Barron for Barclays, was installed at a branch in Enfield, London.
events.significance: The ATM revolutionized personal banking by giving customers access to cash outside normal banking hours and became a global financial fixture.
